description: Core acquisition engine — structured-first source adapters (Wikidata SPARQL, PetScan, official dumps, residual wikitext via mwparserfromhell, generic HTTP fallback) that fetch sweeping cultural/historical/linguistic categories into raw rows with full provenance, behind a uniform adapter interface with caching, rate-limiting, and category-spec input.

userStories.title: Scaffold the culturescrape Python package
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an installable package skeleton so every later subsystem has a home.
acceptanceCriteria: Create pyproject.toml with package name 'culturescrape', Python >=3.11, and dev deps: pytest, mypy, ruff
Create src/culturescrape/__init__.py and src/culturescrape/acquire/__init__.py
`pip install -e .` succeeds in a clean venv
Type checks pass (mypy)
Lint passes (ruff)

userStories.title: Define the RawRecord and Provenance data classes
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a uniform in-memory representation of an acquired row plus its provenance before normalization.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a frozen dataclass Provenance(source, source_url, source_query, retrieved_at, confidence)
Define a dataclass RawRecord(fields: dict[str,str], provenance: Provenance)
retrieved_at is an ISO-8601 UTC string; confidence is a float in [0,1]
Tests pass (pytest) covering construction and validation of out-of-range confidence
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Define the SourceAdapter abstract interface and registry
userStories.description: As a developer, I want every source behind one interface so the orchestrator can call them uniformly.
acceptanceCriteria: Define abstract base SourceAdapter with method fetch(category_spec) -> Iterator[RawRecord]
Define a register/lookup registry keyed by adapter id (e.g. 'wikidata-sparql', 'petscan')
Adapters declare a name and the category-spec source.type they handle
Tests pass (pytest) verifying registry lookup raises a clear error for unknown adapter ids
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the category-spec YAML loader
userStories.description: As a user, I want to declare a category in YAML so a category becomes a reproducible input.
acceptanceCriteria: Parse categories/<name>.yml matching the schema in docs/data-model.md (id, label, description, source, dimensions, links)
Validate required fields and raise a clear error listing missing/invalid keys
Loader returns a typed CategorySpec dataclass
Tests pass (pytest) with a valid fixture and at least two invalid fixtures
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Build an HTTP client with on-disk caching and rate-limiting
userStories.description: As a developer, I need polite, reproducible network access so adapters are testable and don't hammer endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement a client wrapping requests with a configurable per-host rate limit and exponential backoff on 429/5xx
Responses cached on disk keyed by (url, params); cache hits skip the network
A configurable User-Agent string identifies the project (per Wikimedia policy)
Tests pass (pytest) using a mocked transport: cache hit avoids a second call; 429 triggers backoff then retry
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the Wikidata SPARQL adapter
userStories.description: As a user, I want categories defined by a SPARQL query so 'every Peruvian dish' is a query, not a scrape.
acceptanceCriteria: POST/GET the query in category_spec.source.query to query.wikidata.org/sparql with format=json via the cached HTTP client
Map each SPARQL binding row to a RawRecord, preserving the item QID and all selected variables
Set provenance.source='wikidata', source_url to the item URI, source_query to the SPARQL text
Tests pass (pytest) against a recorded SPARQL JSON fixture (no live network)
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the PetScan adapter
userStories.description: As a user, I want to pull Wikipedia category-tree membership lists so categories that live as wiki categories are first-class.
acceptanceCriteria: Call petscan.wmcloud.org with the spec's PetScan parameters (categories, depth, combination, optional WDQS) requesting format=json
Map each result page/item to a RawRecord including title, pageid, and Wikidata QID when present
Set provenance.source='petscan' with the PetScan query URL recorded in source_query
Tests pass (pytest) against a recorded PetScan JSON fixture
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the wikitext adapter using mwparserfromhell
userStories.description: As a user, I want to extract rows from 'List of...' wikitables and infoboxes that SPARQL/PetScan cannot reach.
acceptanceCriteria: Fetch raw wikitext for a page via the MediaWiki API (cached client)
Use mwparserfromhell to extract rows from the first matching wikitable and/or named template parameters specified in the category spec
Each extracted row becomes a RawRecord with provenance.source='wikitext' and the page URL
Tests pass (pytest) parsing a recorded wikitext fixture containing a table and an infobox
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the dump adapter for Getty and Pleiades
userStories.description: As a user, I want to ingest official bulk dumps so authoritative vocabularies can anchor entities.
acceptanceCriteria: Read a local Getty N-Triples dump and emit RawRecords for AAT/TGN/ULAN entries (id, preferred label, type)
Read a local Pleiades JSON/CSV export and emit RawRecords for places (id, name, lat, lon, cross-links)
Provenance records source='getty_aat'|'getty_tgn'|'getty_ulan'|'pleiades' and the record URI; respect ODC-By attribution by storing the license string
Tests pass (pytest) against small recorded dump fixtures for both sources
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement a generic HTTP/HTML fallback adapter
userStories.description: As a user, I want a last-resort adapter for categories that only exist as prose/tables on non-wiki sites.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a URL and a CSS/XPath row+field selector spec, extract rows into RawRecords via the cached client
Adapter is clearly marked best-effort; sets a lower default confidence and source='http'
Robots.txt is checked and respected before fetching
Tests pass (pytest) against a recorded HTML fixture
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add a fetch CLI command
userStories.description: As a user, I want to run a single category from the command line and see raw records written to disk.
acceptanceCriteria: Add console entrypoint `culturescrape fetch <category.yml> --out <dir>`
Command selects the adapter from source.type, runs fetch, and writes raw records as JSON-lines with provenance
Running the command on a fixture-backed category produces a non-empty .jsonl output file
Tests pass (pytest) invoking the CLI with a mocked adapter
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add structured logging and a per-run acquisition report
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see what was fetched, from where, and what failed so runs are auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Emit structured logs (record count, cache hit/miss, retries, errors) per adapter run
Write a run report (JSON) summarizing category id, adapter, row count, distinct sources, and error count
Failures in one record do not abort the whole run; they are counted and logged
Tests pass (pytest) asserting the report counts match a fixture run
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Document adapters and add three example category specs
userStories.description: As a user, I want runnable examples so I can model my own categories.
acceptanceCriteria: Add categories/ examples: peruvian-dishes (wikidata-sparql), us-civil-war-battles (petscan), italian-sculptures (wikidata-sparql)
Add docs/acquisition.md describing each adapter, its source.type, and required spec fields
Each example category validates against the loader (US-004)
Tests pass (pytest) validating all example specs load without error
Lint passes (ruff)
